title: Dynamics of Pure Rolling on Horizontal Surfaces and Directionality of Static Friction
learning_objective: Analyze the direction, magnitude, and role of static friction in maintaining pure rolling under external forces and torques.
explanation: In pure rolling on a horizontal surface at constant velocity without external horizontal forces, the static friction force is exactly zero ($f_s = 0$). When an external horizontal force $F$ is applied to a rolling body at height $h$ relative to its center of mass, static friction acts to enforce the kinematic constraint $a_{\text{cm}} = R \alpha$. Applying dynamical equations: $$F + f_s = M a_{\text{cm}}, \quad F h - f_s R = I_{\text{cm}} \alpha = I_{\text{cm}} \frac{a_{\text{cm}}}{R}$$ Solving simultaneously reveals the magnitude and direction of static friction: $$f_s = F \frac{M R h - I_{\text{cm}}}{I_{\text{cm}} + M R^2} = F \frac{\frac{h}{R} - \frac{k^2}{R^2}}{1 + \frac{k^2}{R^2}}$$ This equation demonstrates three distinct operational regimes: 1. If $h > k^2/R$, static friction acts forward ($f_s > 0$). 2. If $h < k^2/R$, static friction acts backward ($f_s < 0$). 3. If $h = k^2/R$, static friction vanishes identically ($f_s = 0$); this special point is the Center of Percussion. Because the contact point has zero instantaneous velocity, static friction does zero net work in pure rolling: $dW = f_s \cdot (0) = 0$.
intuition: Static friction is an adaptable force—it only pushes in whichever direction is needed to prevent the contact point from slipping! If you pull a spool by a string at the very top, the pull creates so much torque that the bottom tries to kick backward, so friction pushes forward to help it accelerate.
formal_definition: The self-adjusting static friction force at the contact point required to satisfy the non-holonomic constraint equation $a_{\text{cm}} = R \alpha$ under applied loads: $$f_s \le \mu_s N$$
assumptions: Rigid body with radius of gyration k rolling on stationary flat horizontal ground
Applied external force F is purely horizontal at height h above center of mass
Static friction limit f_s <= mu_s M g is not exceeded
boundary_conditions: Valid strictly for pure rolling; if f_s exceeds mu_s N, slipping occurs and dynamic friction f_k = mu_k N applies
source_references: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Chapter 11, Section 11.2 (Forces of Rolling)
Irodov Problems in General Physics, Section 1.4, Problems 1.252-1.255
